## Swarm Gate

- `forge swarm` is `implemented_in_extension`.
- IDE bridge swarm job methods are advertised: cooperative checkpoint cancellation with preserved interrupted worktrees, a scheduler invariant guaranteeing disjoint concurrent write scopes, a swarm-layer write-scope dispatch guard, bounded redacted progress events with reconnect replay, and read-only reconcile with explicit harvest/discard actions.
- Advertised swarm methods: `forge.swarm.apply`, `forge.swarm.cancel`, `forge.swarm.discard`, `forge.swarm.list`, `forge.swarm.reconcile`, `forge.swarm.result`, `forge.swarm.resume`, `forge.swarm.review`, `forge.swarm.start`, `forge.swarm.status`

| `blocked_until_security_model` | `cli_command` | `forge exec` | The broad CLI Forge exec command remains larger than IDE Forge Execute v1 review mode; IDE callers may pass explicit no_log and optional positive max_steps, but auto/fullaccess execution stays blocked until cancellation, sandbox, worker lifecycle, and approval guarantees are stronger. |
| `blocked_until_security_model` | `cli_command` | `forge resume` | forge resume continues an interrupted run by delegating to the sequential execution engine with retries enabled, so it inherits every constraint on broad CLI Forge execution. It also adds a decision of its own: when the plan drifted while the run was dead, --reapprove accepts work that was never approved. That approval belongs in typed IDE UI showing the drift, not in a terminal-scraped flag. |
| `blocked_until_security_model` | `cli_command` | `forge unlock` | forge unlock without --force only clears locks whose owner is provably gone, which is already automatic on acquisition and needs no IDE surface. The command exists for the ambiguous cases, and its one real power -- --force -- is what must not be a button until there is an approval surface for it. |

| `experimental_with_gate` | `cli_forge_chat_command` | `/execute` | Terminal Forge /execute plan drives full-plan parallel mutation.
